title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer, Geospatial Visual Localization
description: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About the Role We are looking for a Research Engineer to help develop our Geospatial Visual Localization technologies, which allows people and robots to accurately localize themselves anywhere on the planet. This is an end-to-end applied research role. You will develop new approaches to open problems alongside our researchers in 3D vision and machine learning, and publish your work at leading conferences. You will help build and train large models on large-scale multi-modal datasets, including our proprietary collection of 30 billion posed images and ship them into production, to be used by people and robots from all over the world. Our team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and other handheld devices, 360 cameras, vehicles, and drones, as well as aerial and satellite imagery, LiDAR, and external geographic data. Your focus will be to improve accuracy and robustness across urban and rural locations, cameras, seasons, weather, and capture quality. The system must remain reliable with noisy GPS, in GPS-denied environments, and with outdated reference maps. Each pose estimate comes with an uncertainty that our customers rely on, and keeping it well calibrated across these conditions is part of the work. What You'll Do Design, implement, and evaluate novel visual localization algorithms, combining 3D vision and deep learning. Train large models on multi-modal data at scale, and build the benchmarks that measure their accuracy and robustness. Develop robust solutions for difficult real-world conditions: noisy or denied GPS, changing appearance, varying capture quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Work side-by-side with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping, as well as engineering and product teams, to identify the highest-impact problems and turn research into end-to-end solutions that operate at production scale. Communicate results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, internal presentations, and publications. What You'll Bring Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, deep learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience with multi-view geometry and related problems, such as camera pose estimation, monocular depth estimation, SfM, SLAM, georeferencing, point-cloud registration, or sensor fusion. Knowledge of transformer models for 3D vision, such as vision foundation models, feed-forward 3D reconstruction, or multi-view and multi-modal attention. Knowledge of geospatial data and coordinate reference systems. Ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose appropriate mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience training deep learning models at scale, with libraries such as PyTorch, NumPy, and SciPy. Strong software engineering skills, with the ability to turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. Experience taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication and the ability to collaborate across research and engineering disciplines. Nice to Have A PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field, or equivalent research or industry experience. A PhD is not required. A strong publication record or substantial active involvement in the research community, especially at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, SIGGRAPH Asia, 3DV, ICRA, RSS, or related conferences and journals. Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, IMUs, LiDAR data, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data. Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. Location & Work Model This role is based in our London office, with three days per week in office. Inclusive Application We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed - you may be exactly who we're looking for. Equal Opportunity Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process. Candidate Privacy I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice . title: Developer Experience / DevEx
description: About Fractile Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. About the Software organisation at Fractile Developer Experience sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing. About the team and role The Developer Experience team at Fractile helps shape how our customers interact with the Fractile inference accelerator. We work across the company to identify, create, and present information on how the system is being used, as well as providing the tooling to help optimise our customers' usage of the system, while keeping a shallow learning curve. As a member of the Developer Experience team you will need to understand the current state of development for inference hardware. You will need to be able to identify what will work well for engineers wanting to identify potential opportunities for performance improvements, while knowing what tooling will fit into an existing LLM engineer's workflow with the minimal amount of disruption and effort. About you We're looking for someone who is self-driven and capable of identifying tooling opportunities, designing those tools, and delivering them in a way which will fit in with an LLM engineer's existing toolset. You will have worked in this area before, possibly as an FDE or at a company that provides inference services using their own models, and have the ability to develop new tools that are designed to be functional and easy to learn and use. Key Requirements Experience with inference frameworks such as JAX and/or PyTorch Experience of software development in Python, Rust, C/C++, or a similar language Experience monitoring and optimising code written in CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, or similar Experience monitoring and optimising LLM deployments with 50+ billion parameters Experience working with stakeholders across multiple teams What We Offer Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role. Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance. Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment. Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We’ve recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us! Export controls Our work involves technologies subject to UK, US and other international export control regulations. Certain roles may require additional eligibility checks to ensure compliance with applicable law. We'll be transparent about this throughout the hiring process. Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you. The Knowledge Platform team builds Exa's knowledge engine. We continuously synthesize information from across the web and beyond into one of the world's largest open-domain knowledge graphs, with hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims. The work has two halves: construction pipelines that decide what to trust, and retrieval engines that decide how best to search it. Our goal is to give agents answers to any factual question about the world with unprecedented precision and completeness. In this role, you'll own the query engine that searches hundreds of billions of claims across a variety of retrieval backends, from a distributed graph database to vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial indexes. This is greenfield work with a massive scope. No off-the-shelf system answers precise questions over hundreds of billions of evidence-backed claims at agent speed, so you'll make foundational decisions, from storage layout and indexing across engines to the query language and the planner that routes work between them, that every query depends on. What you'll do Own storage and indexing across backends: data layout, partitioning and indexes for graph, vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval, with bulk snapshot builds and live ingest that never take the system down. Decide how best to search: cost-based planning from cardinality estimates that chooses, for each question, which backends to use, in what order and how to join their results, executed as traversals, retrievals, filters and aggregations in one plan. Make it fast at scale: serve thousands of queries per second, profiling and cutting p50/p99 latency, memory and cost per query under high concurrent load, from on-disk layout to network fan-out. Keep answers consistent while the data converges: the graph is fed by live updates and bulk snapshots at once and is eventually consistent by design, so you'll own what a query may see while it converges: consistent snapshot promotion, ordered application of live updates and stable pagination across versions. Measure precision and completeness: end-to-end checks every deployment must pass, plus evals and metrics that show when a plan returns wrong results or misses ones it should have found. What we're looking for You've worked deep inside a distributed database, query engine, search engine or storage system. Strong grasp of indexing, query planning and optimization, and storage formats. Solid grasp of distributed systems fundamentals: consensus, replication, sharding and fault tolerance. Strong in a systems language (Go, Rust or C++). You profile before you optimize, and you've shipped measured latency wins in production. You obsess over correctness, reliability and data quality as much as scale. Bonus Graph databases, or combining vector, full-text, time-series and geospatial retrieval Compilers, query language design or cost-based optimizers Example projects Build a system that retrieves and reasons over everything known about any company or person in the world, answering any factual question precisely and completely. Answer precise multi-hop questions over hundreds of billions of claims at thousands of QPS with interactive latency. Build a planner that picks the right mix of graph, vector, full-text and geospatial retrieval for any question, and proves it chose well. Make new knowledge queryable seconds after it's synthesized, without ever serving an inconsistent result. Logistics Location: This is an in-person opportunity in Zurich. title: Research Engineer, Content Understanding
description: Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z. Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you. As a backend engineer, you'd play a critical role in our search architecture. We're pretty flexible on what projects people work on based on their skills and interests. Search quality is bounded by what we understand about a page. Before anything can be retrieved, something has to work out what the page actually says. That means parsing it into the parts that are content and the parts that are furniture, classifying what kind of page it is and what it is about, telling whether the page is usable at all, extracting when it was published, judging how good it is and whether it can be trusted, and working out whether it says anything that a page we already have does not. All of this has to work on every page on the web, in every language, in every shape the web comes in. Some of this is classic document understanding. Some of it is much more open. Credibility and misinformation, AI-generated and machine-spun content, and pages written to be found rather than read are all unsolved, and search results are only as trustworthy as our answers to them. We are looking for a research engineer to work on this. There is a lot of room to do it well. Desired Experience Graduate-level ML experience (Master’s or PhD with at least 2 years of relevant experience), or an exceptionally strong undergrad You can build a transformer from scratch in PyTorch, and you have trained models that then had to be cheap enough to run everywhere You like building large-scale datasets and living in the data. Most of the wins here are in the supervision rather than the architecture You are comfortable with problems where the ground truth does not exist yet and defining it is part of the job You care about the problem of finding high quality knowledge and recognize how important this is for the world Example Projects Make parsing work on the pages where it currently does not, and prove the improvement rather than assert it Teach a model to judge page quality, and get everyone to agree on what quality means well enough to supervise it Work on credibility and misinformation as a modelling problem: what a page claims, whether it is a reliable source of it, and whether it was written for a reader or for a crawler Decide whether two documents are semantically the same or genuinely different, so we can deduplicate the web without collapsing pages that a user would want to see separately Build classification and extraction that is accurate at web scale and cheap enough to run on all of it Design the supervision for something nobody has labels for, and find out whether it is learnable at all Trace a bad search result back to the page-level prediction that caused it, and fix it at the source Exa is an equal opportunity employer. We are in an active build phase: a small, growing team turning lab setups into a tool that does not exist anywhere else yet. The role As Embedded Engineer you own everything between the instrument hardware and our acquisition software. You integrate cameras, frame grabbers, motion controllers, piezo stages, lasers and FPGA timing hardware, and you make them run as one synchronized, reliable scan. The work is hands-on: vendor SDKs, trigger wiring, PCIe cards and lab networks one day, clean driver code and a live data stream to the user interface the next. You work closely with the System, Mechatronics, Application and Algorithm engineers. What you will do Design the trigger and acquisition architecture that synchronizes camera exposure, stage motion and laser pulses. Integrate industrial cameras and frame grabbers through industry-standard interfaces and vendor SDKs, from driver set-up to stable high-rate acquisition. Integrate motion controllers and positioning stages through vendor APIs and controller scripting, including commissioning and tuning with the Mechatronics Engineer. Develop and extend FPGA-based timing and I/O for triggering and position-synchronized acquisition. Write driver and control layers in C/C++ and Python that the scan and reconstruction software builds on, and expose live status and data streams to the user interface. Own the instrument PC and lab network set-up: PCIe hardware, high-speed Ethernet links between devices, IP planning and device discovery. Bring up and debug hardware in the lab with oscilloscope, logic analyzer and network captures, and document interfaces and timing budgets with the System Engineer. Take part in code review and help move the set-up from prototype to a reproducible, maintainable tool. Your profile MSc in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Applied Physics or a related field. ~5 years of hands-on experience integrating and controlling hardware, preferably in high-tech equipment, scientific instruments or industrial automation. Strong C/C++ and Python, including working with vendor SDKs and drivers on Windows and Linux. Proven experience with hardware triggering and synchronization of multiple devices (cameras, motion, lasers, DAQ). Experience with FPGA development or working closely with FPGA-based timing hardware. Solid grasp of hardware interfaces and networking: Ethernet, USB, serial, PCIe, and multi-device lab networks. Comfortable in the lab: reading schematics, using an oscilloscope and logic analyzer, and debugging where hardware and software meet. Experience with Git and collaborative code review. Full professional proficiency in English. We value judgment and ownership over a perfect match. If you recognize yourself in most of this, we would like to hear from you. Bonus Experience with machine-vision cameras, frame grabbers or high-throughput image acquisition. Experience with precision motion controllers and encoder-based position triggering. High-speed data paths to a host PC, SoC FPGAs or Linux driver development. Experience building lightweight web or API layers for instrument control and live data. Background in optics, lasers, coherent imaging, semiconductor metrology or lithography equipment. Experience with CI, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or working in a Scrum team. What we offer Ownership of the embedded and timing backbone of a tool that does not exist anywhere else yet. A small team with short feedback loops and real impact on the product. Hands-on work at the meeting point of hardware, optics and software, on the High Tech Campus Eindhoven. A competitive salary for the Dutch market. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. These decisions are worth more than most ranking work. The cheapest way to improve search is to stop indexing pages nobody should ever retrieve, and to start indexing the ones we are missing. title: Certification Engineer
description: About EH Energy Engineering EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners. To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready. This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland . We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements , so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate . Key responsibilities Certification strategy and project management Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine) Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT) Safety engineering and risk analysis Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882) Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports Compliance and technical documentation Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates Collaboration and continuous improvement Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations). Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical) Standards and regulatory scope The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 Required qualifications Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine) Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110 Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508 Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals Fluent English, written and spoken Preferred qualifications and personal profile Nice to have Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification Personal profile Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end Start date: Immediately Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow
